items.title: 1500 jobs to go: David Jones staff set to learn their fate this week
paras: Advertisement Business Companies David Jones collapse 1500 jobs to go: David Jones staff set to learn their fate this week Jessica Yun Updated November 18, 2026 — 12:19pm , first published 11:59am
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.
Share A A A About 1500 David Jones workers are bracing to be told later this week that they have lost their jobs as the department store’s receivers prepare to permanently close 19 stores.

Representatives for retail worker union SDA (Shop, Distributive and Allied Employees Association) met with receivers from FTI Consulting late last week and were advised only 170 roles, or 10 per cent, would be saved from 1689 jobs lost as a result of the closure of 18 stores in Australia and one in New Zealand .

With seven stores in NSW set to shut, more than 600 of the 1500 roles at risk of disappearing are based in the state, most of whom work in customer service. Jeremy Piper With seven stores in NSW set to shut, more than 600 roles set to disappear are based in the state, most of whom work in customer service.
“We’re very disappointed with the very low number of 170 redeployments,” Smith told this masthead on Wednesday morning.
“We’re talking about a very low number, compared to the number of redundancies … It’s a missed opportunity to reset service levels at David Jones.”
In an initial creditor’s meeting yesterday morning , David Jones’ administrators said an employee consultation process was underway and indicated impacted staff would find out “in the coming days”.

In NSW, David Jones employs about 120 staff in its Macquarie Centre store, 100 at its Hornsby store and roughly 115 at Warringah Mall, in Sydney’s northern beaches. Parramatta employs about 90 staff while Wollongong has about 85 employees. David Jones in Campbelltown hires approximately 80 workers. Green Hills hires about 50 workers.
In Victoria, there is a total of about 250 employees in the three stores set to shut - Malvern Central, Highpoint and Glen Waverley.
The 170 redeployed roles will be predominantly in beauty and cosmetics counters at other stores, Smith said, as well as a limited number of roles in sales and management.
“We’ll keep working with receivers to see if we can change that number, but it doesn’t look positive so far,” Smith said.
“You’ve got to have enough staff on the floor to take the money off the customers who want to give it to you. If you don’t have enough staff, you don’t turn the business around.”
The SDA has contacted a number of other retailers as well as the bus industry to see where David Jones workers can be retrained or hired elsewhere.
“It’s a tight time hiring now. Christmas hiring has already been done,” said Smith.
“Post-Christmas when it’s notoriously a quiet time in retail, we’ll still be able to fill vacancies and take people on.

items.title: Banks weigh down ASX, miners rebound
paras: Advertisement Updated Business Markets World markets Banks weigh down ASX, miners rebound Staff writers Updated November 18, 2026 — 11:06am , first published November 18, 2026 — 5:12am
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Share A A A The Australian sharemarket has retreated at the open after Wall Street wobbled again as AI stocks led widespread losses before Nvidia reported better-than-expected results after the closing bell.

The S&P/ASX 200 was down 22.4 points or 0.3 per cent in early trade, with nine of 11 industry sectors in negative territory. Mining stocks are higher, as they clawed back some of Tuesday’s heavy losses . The AFR Real Economy index was down 4.3 points or 0.4 per cent to 1028.01.

Nvidia’s results landed after the closing bell. AP Financial stocks lost ground with Commonwealth Bank and Westpac down 1.2 per cent, ANZ down 1.8 per cent and National Australia Bank down 1.7 per cent.

Mining stocks largely rebounded from the previous session’s heavy losses in early trade on Wednesday with BHP up 1.7 per cent and Fortescue up 1.2 per cent, but Rio Tinto dipped 0.2 per cent. Gold stocks advanced, with Northern Star up 1.3 per cent and Evolution Mining up 0.5 per cent.

Oil steadied as traders assessed renewed fighting in the Middle East against signs of recovering supplies and higher US inventories. West Texas Intermediate traded near $US86 a barrel while Brent closed above $US93. Energy stocks are mixed, with Woodside, Ampol and Santos flat in early trade while Yancoal was up 2 per cent and Whitehaven Coal was up 2.7 per cent.

Software company Nuix soared 54.7 per cent after announcing it has received a takeover bid from US-based private equity firm Haveli Investments Software Fund. Technology stocks are mixed overall, with TechnologyOne down 4.9 per cent, Xero down 1.7 per cent and WiseTech down 0.3 per cent but NEXTDC and Megaport each are up 1.2 per cent.

On Wall Street, the S&P 500 sank 1 per cent and at one point was on track for its first back-to-back losses of at least 1.5 per cent since March. The Dow Jones dropped 848 points, or 1.6 per cent, and the Nasdaq composite fell 0.7 per cent.

The centre of the action was again Nvidia which jumped 5 per cent in after-hours trade after it forecast quarterly revenue above Wall Street estimates, giving investors some relief after longtime leader Jensen Huang’s resignation plunged the chip firm into crisis.

Huang said earlier on the X social-media network that he would come back as CEO if “the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America” but Nvidia’s new chairman Harvey Jones told investors during the earnings call that the company’s board of directors did not intend to reinstate Huang.

Other AI stocks also swung sharply. Advanced Micro Devices went from an early gain of 1.6 per cent to a drop of 4.7 per cent before trimming its fall to 0.2 per cent. CoreWeave initially climbed 1.8 per cent, flipped to a loss of 6.1 per cent and then finished nearly unchanged.

AI-related stocks have been shaky for months because of a rolling chain of worries. At first, it was concerns that AI stock prices had broadly shot too high in their frenzy. Then it was worries that high interest rates would mean less borrowed money to fund further growth. More recently, it was concerns that Democratic victories in this month’s US midterm elections could mean tougher regulations and restrictions on AI data centres.
Such stocks can almost single-handedly set the US market’s course because they’ve grown into some of Wall Street’s most valuable and most influential.
Most of Wall Street was weak, as 17 out of every 20 stocks within the index fell,
Home Depot sank 2.4 per cent even though it reported profit for the latest quarter that edged past analysts’ expectations.
The retailer has been hampered by a housing market chilled by expensive mortgage rates, which have climbed with Treasury yields because of high oil prices, high inflation and other factors.

The 10-year Treasury yield climbed toward 5.15 per cent Tuesday morning from 5.12 per cent late Monday before later pulling back to 5.10 per cent. It erased its gain after the sharp drops for AI stocks pushed investors to herd into investments seen as safer bets.

In the morning, yields got support from a report showing better growth in an underlying measure of spending at US retailers than economists expected. Such spending, along with big investments in AI, has helped the US economy continue to grow despite frustration with high inflation.
Elsewhere on Wall Street, stocks of banks fell amid concerns about how much pain the broad US economy will feel from any pullback in AI-related spending.
JPMorgan Chase fell 2.4 per cent. A day before, a technical issue at the bank had slowed transactions for customers trying to use the Zelle payment system.
Apple and Marriott had only modest moves following outages in their systems. Apple slipped 0.2 per cent, and Marriott International fell 0.7 per cent.

United Airlines had its own operational struggles, as a system outage forced the carrier to delay departing flights Monday. That came just days after a malfunction in the Federal Aviation Administration’s network prompted a nationwide ground stop.
United’s stock lost 4 per cent, but it was also hurt by a rise in oil prices.
The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil rose 0.8 per cent to $US93.14. It’s been yo-yoing amid uncertainty about what will happen in the war with Iran.

The downward momentum on Wall Street was strong enough to erase early gains for The Walt Disney Co. and pull it down 1.5 per cent, even though it reported stronger revenue for the latest quarter than analysts expected.

Stock prices generally tend to follow the path of corporate profits over the long term, depending on how interest rates behave. The big businesses across the S&P 500 index are on track to deliver earnings per share for the summer that are nearly 32 per cent higher than a year earlier, according to FactSet.

items.title: Australia faces 20-plus years of lost wage growth
paras: Every three months, the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) releases new forecasts for the next two years in its Statement on Monetary Policy (SoMP). These forecasts provide a snapshot of where the RBA believes things are heading across a range of factors, from investment and consumer spending to unemployment, wage growth, and inflation.
The November SoMP projected minimal improvement in real wages, which, by the end of 2028, will still be tracking at around late-2011 levels:
Greg Jericho, chief economist at the Australia Institute, posted an article at The Point extrapolating the RBA’s real wage forecasts, suggesting real wages might not recover until around 2044.

items.title: Cambridge Dictionary names 'human' word of the year in rebuttal to AI
paras: The Cambridge Dictionary's choice is linked to the rising influence of artificial intelligence. ( Reuters: Dado Ruvic )
One of the words to watch for next year is FOBO, meaning "fear of becoming obsolete", because jobs can be performed by AI.
The word "human" has been named Cambridge Dictionary's Word of the Year, in a pointed illustration of the rising influence of artificial intelligence.
The definition in the dictionary is to have the "qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines".
Cambridge University Press board member Francesca Woodward said that in an era of rapidly expanding AI and dire warnings it could even wipe out humanity, the word captured "the 2026 Zeitgeist".
She said over the past 12 months, people had been "really considering what it is to be human", in particular due to concerns about AI taking over their jobs.
There are concerns about AI taking over their jobs. ( Reuters/Dado Ruvic/Illustration )
"I think people are trying to remind themselves of … what human means," she said.
The word beat other words related to AI and the online world, reflecting intense global interest in how technology is changing our lives, she said.
Ms Woodward said that the dictionary's lexicographers had also observed an increased used of "human" in compound words such as human-made or human author.
Cambridge University philosopher of science Tom McClelland said "human" was a "really interesting choice".
Humanoids, which combine AI and robotics, have become more competent. ( AFP: Leung Man Hei )

"We're trying to understand the difference between a human mind and an artificial mind, between living beings like us and artificial beings that we're creating. What sets us apart? Is it consciousness, creativity or compassion?"
The focus on what it means to be human has seen global leaders and prominent figures such as Pope Leo XIV, Bill Gates, classicist Mary Beard and actor Cate Blanchett weigh in on the debate.
Other contenders for the word of the year crown included "agent", meaning "an artificial intelligence system that can operate in a complicated way without human control".
Also in the running was "wholesome", defined as "good for you, and likely to improve your life either physically, morally, or emotionally".
"Dusking" is the the practice of watching daylight turn to darkness as a form of relaxation. ( Supplied: Kodi Wright )
"Dusking" was also in contention, the practice of watching daylight turn to darkness as a form of relaxation.
It is a Dutch tradition, which has been revived as a way of reconnecting with the natural world.

Other new words added to the dictionary in 2026 included "aura farming", doing things to show a personality that people will admire, and "looksmaxing", making yourself as physically attractive as possible.
The word of the year and new additions are selected using a range of criteria, including the words searched for on the Cambridge Dictionary website.
Among words to watch for next year, according to Cambridge Dictionary, were FOBO, "fear of becoming obsolete", because your job can be performed by AI.
Another was "weather whiplash", which means a "quick change from one extreme of weather to another".
Last year's word of the year was "parasocial", to describe the sense of having a connection to a famous person you do not know personally or a fictional character.

items.title: Routine dental check-up spots tongue cancer and saves woman's life
paras: Monica Frain credits Broome dentist Stephanie Mulcahy with saving her life after spotting incipient tongue cancer. ( ABC Kimberley: Natasha Clark )
A West Australian woman has recounted how a regular dental check-up in 2022 saved her life.
Monica Frain had a pin-head sized lump on her tongue, which her dentist helped identify as cancerous.
The Broome case has highlighted the importance of regular dentist check-ups.
A routine trip to the dentist took an unexpected turn for a West Australian woman, ending in life-saving surgery to remove part of her tongue.
Broome resident Monica Frain felt "annoyed" but not alarmed by the pinhead-sized lump on her tongue that had been bothering her for months in late 2022.
Having recently undergone cardiac surgery, she thought the minuscule lump was the result of a breathing tube being placed down her throat during the procedure.
When Monica Frain showed a minuscule lump to a GP, the doctor dismissed it and suggested she bite it off. ( ABC Kimberley: Natasha Clark )
Ms Frain showed the lump to a local GP, who said it was nothing to worry about and suggested she bite it off.
But during a dental check-up, dentist Stephanie Mulcahy saw the lump and immediately referred Ms Frain to an oral medicine specialist.
"While it didn't look sinister, I wanted confirmation on what it was," Dr Mulcahy said.
Access to specialists can be hard to come by in Broome and other communities across WA's far northern Kimberley.
Most fly from Perth, 2,240 kilometres south, on a strict rotating schedule.
For Ms Frain, getting a diagnosis required a flight to Perth at the start of 2023.
Her biopsy results showed she had squamous carcinoma, the most common form of tongue cancer.
The cancer, thankfully, had not spread, with only surgery required for treatment.
But it still involved the removal of more than a third of Ms Frain's tongue.
She said she was 'extremely grateful' for Dr Mulcahy's quick response and diagnosis.
"If Dr Steph had not pushed for me to go and see a specialist and have it removed I could have been in a terrible state," she said.
Monica Frain credits Dr Mulcahy's insistence she have her tongue examined by an oral medicine specialist with saving her life. ( Natasha Clark )
Dr Mulcahy said she knew firsthand what happened when cancers were left to advance, having immediately identified tongue cancer in patients, including one whose disease proved fatal.
But Ms Frain's experience also reflects the barriers regional patients face when accessing specialist care.
Available assistance for regional and remote patients in WA is also limited compared to other states.
Health Consumers Council WA chief executive officer Clare Mullen said West Australians living regionally should not face heightened obstacles in accessing specialist healthcare.
"People living regionally should be able to have the confidence if they need access to specialist healthcare, they'll be able to access it," she said.
"Obviously, WA's geography presents some logistical challenges, but that same geography is also a source of significant wealth, which should make it easier to fund the solutions."
Oral and maxillofacial pathology specialist Omar Kujan said Ms Frain's story and Dr Mulcahy's quick action and referral highlighted the importance of timely care.
"Regular dental check-ups can save lives by identifying early warning signs that people may not notice themselves," Dr Kujan said.
Omar Kujan says for people living in remote and regional areas dental check-ups are essential for early detection of oral cancer. ( supplied )
"Oral cancer can develop without pain or obvious symptoms, and early diagnosis significantly improves the chances of successful treatment and survival.
"Timely access to oral healthcare must be a priority, particularly in regional and remote Australia."

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "India matters most for future of planet" says British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): In recent times when climate change has become a pressing issue with countries across the world being ravaged due to climate catastrophes, it becomes imperative to discuss and deliberate upon global actions that can help the world rise up and meet these challenges. At the NDTV World Summit's a discussion was held on the theme, "India Matters The Most For Future Of Planet". Participants in the discussion included Erik Solheim, Former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway; Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India; Shishir Priyadarshi, President Chintan Research Foundation; Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. "India is the country that matters the most for the future of the planet and climate change. India's ambition for development should not in any way be constrained by the responsibilities of the planet," Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India, emphasised. She noted that the UK is committed towards the Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) reforms, technology and research support in India to aid the efforts. "Every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure pays 4 times over," said Cameron. "Lived experience of climate emergencies helps people to understand why their government needs to take policy action now," she added. Further talking about the need for urgent government action, Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said, "Series of disasters affecting both developed and developing countries are serving as a wake-up call. As rich countries will get more and more affected by climate change which they did not imagine till a couple of years ago, most vulnerable countries are going to be struggling with impacts who also have very less capacity to deal with it. India is taking a leadership role in the global fight against climate change. Initiatives such as Global Biofuels Alliance, International Solar Alliance, and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure are some efforts taken by India in recent years to manage the climate crisis. (ANI)

items.title: India is the top market for investment globally: Mark Mobius
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Mark Mobius, Founder of Mobius Capital Partners LLP , and an ace investor with expertise in emerging markets said, India's is the top stock market globally where he would like to invest. In an exclusive interview with ANI, the octagenarian said, "India would have to come first when I think about investment," Mobius stated, "Of course, India would have to be the first choice. Then, I would probably look at Taiwan. It's a Chinese society, but it's a free society and they're doing very well. Now we're beginning to see China rise again. There will be some interesting companies in China, but still, India remains our top pick." Mobius highlighted technology as his favorite sector to invest in India. "In the future, I believe there's going to be significant growth in hardware technology. As you know, India is already strong in software technology, but moving forward, hardware manufacturing will gain momentum here in India," he said. Discussing India's semiconductor infrastructure, Mobius mentioned that it is already developing. "Many of the world's large semiconductor companies already have software development operations in India, employing thousands of software engineers. The next step, of course, is hardware. Soon, we'll see large semiconductor manufacturing plants. The scale of investment we're talking about isn't in the millions, but billions of dollars, to produce the most advanced semiconductors in the world." Mobius also fondly remembered Ratan Tata, who passed away this month. "I met him many years ago and found him to be a very friendly, humble, and insightful person. I was deeply saddened to hear about his passing. I considered him one of the great Indian entrepreneurs of the century," Mobius added. Earlier on Monday, Mark Mobius, speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2024, reiterated he was bullish on India's real estate and semiconductor sectors, as he outlined the potential of these two key industries. In the semiconductor space, he said fabrication companies (fabs) will come here because India has got the population and the labour force. The octagenarian believes India will become "the leader" of the semiconductor industry. The government has so far approved five semiconductor units in India, of which construction in two sites is on, and soon the work in the other three will start. The companies have already made a cumulative investment of almost Rs 1.5 lakh crore. While talking about the parameters he looks at while investing in companies, Mobius said he looks at the growth of earnings in companies, along with the return on capital invested, and the quality of management. Asked about his investment advice to his "younger self," Mobius said, "Don't be in a rush, and study carefully". He added that one has to listen to the market. (ANI)

items.title: Mukka Proteins Limited Announces Rs 98 Crore Preferential Issue for Acquisition and Expansion
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel VMPL Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: Mukka Proteins Limited , India's largest fish meal and insect meal producer and a leader in the animal protein industry , has announced the approval of a preferential issue worth Rs 98 crore by its Board of Directors. This strategic move will help Mukka Proteins in its ongoing domestic and international acquisition and expansion efforts, reinforcing its position in the global market. A significant portion of the funding will come from the promoter and promoter group, underlining their commitment to the company's robust growth strategy. The preferential issue will comprise up to 1.96 crore equity shares at Rs50 per share, aggregating to Rs98 crore. This price includes a premium of Rs49 per share on the face value of Rs1. Mukka Proteins will use the raised capital to enhance production capabilities and meet the growing global demand for sustainable and high-quality protein solutions, particularly in the fishmeal and insect meal sectors. In a clear show of confidence, Mukka Proteins' promoters have committed to a capital infusion of INR 60 crore through a preferential allotment of equity shares. This significant financial backing will be used to strengthen the company's financial position, reduce debt, and fund key operational improvements. Mukka Proteins has consistently embraced sustainability, having commercialized insect protein as a significant innovation for the aquaculture and animal feed industry. The company's waste-to-food initiatives have contributed to environmental sustainability, particularly in collaboration with the Mangaluru municipality for waste management. These efforts not only align with global environmental best practices but also enhance circular economy processes, focusing on converting municipal waste into valuable protein and oil products. Mukka Proteins is known for its strong commitment to ecological preservation, evident through the development of sustainable products such as fishmeal, fish oil, and insect protein. As a key player in the aquaculture and nutraceutical markets, Mukka contributes 25-30% of the market share in India's fishmeal and fish oil industry. The company plans to expand its operations further, capitalizing on this capital infusion to enter new markets and enhance its global footprint.

This issuance is subject to necessary statutory and regulatory approvals, including shareholder approval at the upcoming Extra-Ordinary General Meeting (EGM) on November 16, 2024. Managing Director and CEO Harris commented, "This preferential issue is a major milestone for Mukka Proteins as we continue to strengthen our market position. Our growth plans remain firmly rooted in sustainability, and this capital will enable us to scale up production, diversify our product offerings, and reinforce our commitment to responsible and eco-friendly business practices." Mukka Proteins Limited is poised to capture new opportunities in the animal protein sector, reinforcing its legacy of innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence. Mukka Proteins Limited : Mukka Proteins Limited is a leading manufacturer and exporter of fish meal , fish oil, and other protein products. The company has built a reputation for delivering high-quality, sustainable protein products to a global customer base. With a commitment to innovation and quality, Mukka Proteins serves industries including aquaculture, pet food, and agriculture across multiple continents. Headquartered in Mangalore, India, Mukka Proteins operates state-of-the-art processing facilities that meet stringent international standards. The company is dedicated to sustainable practices and has been at the forefront of environmental stewardship within the protein processing industry. (ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by VMPL . ANI will not be responsible in any way for the content of the same)

items.title: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
paras: Pushing Plugins Copilot is “the new OS for work,” and now Office runs inside of it Word, Excel, and PowerPoint now live inside Copilot; always-on agents are next.

41 ... ... ... Credit: Microsoft Stream Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company’s vision for its new “frontier ecosystem,” announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as “the new OS for work.”

The announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent’s work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications.

The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the company first announced in September. Parts of that vision are now becoming “generally available,” as Nadella puts it, with autonomous agents and new governance tools arriving alongside them.

Copilot Autopilot (not to be confused with Windows Autopilot) is a “persistent, proactive agent for personal productivity” according to Microsoft. In a nutshell, Autopilot is a cloud-based autonomous AI agent that users can delegate responsibilities to, not just single tasks. Autopilot can be authorized to work across services like email and calendars and complete tasks assigned to it as part of its role. Autopilot will use usage-based billing via Copilot Credits, but final pricing has not been announced ahead of general availability.

Also announced as generally available at the keynote speech was Microsoft IQ , an intelligence platform that houses Work IQ , a context layer that helps agents understand a company’s communications, relationships, and ongoing work. Nadella described Work IQ as perhaps a company’s most valuable database: “It has a deep understanding of the people, their relationships to other people, your emails, your meetings, chats, projects that make up all the fabric of work.” Whether companies want autonomous agents to have access to internal documents and messaging data will have to be determined by their own internal IT review.

Copilot Workspaces is a collaborative environment currently available through Microsoft’s Frontier early-access program, but coming soon will be the ability to bring personal Autopilot agents into Workspaces. Early in the keynote address, Nadella said that “Until now, AI interactions have mostly been single-player. Workspaces makes it a truly multiplayer experience, where people and agents drive towards a common goal, with shared context.”

Trust, the third pillar of Microsoft’s new frontier ecosystem, was something that Nadella continued returning to during his presentation, and not in a way that some might expect. “We find ourselves in a place where alignment is elusive. Mechanistic understanding of these models is elusive. The question is: How can you even trust all this powerful technology? The reality is, by definition, you can’t,” he said.

In a departure from the norms of “AI is magic” corporate hype sentiment, Nadella conceded that the internal workings of AI thought processes remain difficult to understand, and models cannot be trusted to govern themselves, regardless of whether their answers are accurate. Nadella described the solution as “an architectural imperative to separate the supply of intelligence” from the authority granted to it. Microsoft says each Autopilot agent will have a unique ID, and administrators can restrict permissions or block it entirely. All agent activities are logged for human review, and Autopilot can ask for human approval before engaging in certain actions.

The promised agent controls and admission that AI systems can’t always be trusted are meaningful, but Microsoft is asking businesses and users to place their trust in the company’s own safeguards instead, though the effectiveness of those safeguards against mistakes, rogue actions, or data exposure will still have to be demonstrated. In Microsoft’s view, the solution to untrustworthy intelligence is not to make AI agents trustworthy, but to control what they’re permitted to do. Businesses will have to decide how much autonomy they delegate to agents.

Along with the guardrails, Microsoft announced what it calls the “ AI Transparency Initiative .” The effort has partnered with 40-plus major companies, including Adobe and Mastercard, to develop open, industrywide standards for AI governance and security. Nadella described the initiative as a way for industry to “help establish an open standard that makes AI safer, more transparent, and more accessible.”

Along with the other announced additions, Microsoft also announced expanding capabilities for Agent 365 , its existing control plane for managing AI agents across enterprise environments. The new agent sheriff extends existing identity, security, and management systems to AI agents. Microsoft describes the objective as providing “observability at every layer of the stack.” Agent 365 offers governance controls over agent behavior in what Microsoft says is “autonomous in execution, but bounded and supervised.”

Along with Agent 365 comes Agent 365 Business Analytics : “You can simply think of this as an ERP system of AI usage. You can see exactly what’s driving the spend and connect the spend to the outcomes that drive business value,” said Nadella. Customers will be able to see real-world costs associated with AI token-spend, and compare those metrics to the value of work performed. Microsoft acknowledged that the estimations of assisted work hours are determined by a model , and not a direct measurement of time that may have been saved. This is a telling concession for Microsoft to make as businesses evaluate whether there will be an ROI on AI implementations, but according to Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft Commercial Business, “anything you can do with Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot, for less .”

Nadella offered only a brief acknowledgment of last week’s outage that disrupted access to services like Exchange Online and Teams for users across the globe. “Last week was a reminder of how critical digital infrastructure is as the dial tone for the world,” he said. “We know the trust you place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously, and in that context I know we have work to do.”

That statement was all the time the elephant in the room was given, but Microsoft did seem to acknowledge the public’s growing concern over data center projects by highlighting the previously discussed “ community-first AI infrastructure plan .” Not a surprise in a presentation that asks organizations to extend more autonomy to software agents, at a time when Microsoft’s existing infrastructure is under increased scrutiny.

items.title: San Diego dumps both Flock cameras and smart streetlights
paras: shut down San Diego dumps both Flock cameras and smart streetlights 500+ cameras will go dark just 3 years after mayor urged approval.

25 ... ... ... Credit: Getty Images | Smith Collection/Gado Credit: Getty Images | Smith Collection/Gado Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav On Monday evening, San Diego’s city council voted to end its contracts with two surveillance equipment vendors, Flock and Ubicquia. San Diego is one of the largest cities to end its relationship with Flock , the startup with an estimated valuation of $8.3 billion.
“We fucking won!” Lily Irani of the Transparent and Responsible Use of Surveillance Technology (TRUST) SD Coalition told Ars.
She and her colleagues have been among the loudest critics in recent years.

“The national energy creating left and right and center coalitions was the major cause [of the political victory],” she said, noting that it was only last month that one of the councilmembers revoked his support , creating an opening for a political majority to halt the surveillance.
That council member, Stephen Whitburn, said in an October press conference that he wanted his fellow citizens to “feel safe.”
“If Flock cameras are causing many San Diegans to feel unsafe, then they have lost effectiveness as a public safety tool,” he said at the time.

After the Monday vote, San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria said in a social media post that he “respect[ed] the Council’s decision” and would not veto the move to stop operation of the cameras across the city.

Andrew Smith, a spokesperson for Flock, told Ars in an email on Tuesday that the company also “respect[s] the city’s decision.” But Flock isn’t happy about it. “When a tool that is actively helping solve violent crimes is removed, public safety moves backward,” Smith wrote. “That has real consequences: cases will take longer to solve, organized retail theft crews will operate with fewer obstacles, a missing child may not be returned home, and victims may wait longer, or indefinitely, for justice.”
At Monday’s city council meeting, police representatives said there has been a 20 percent decline in vehicle theft since 2023, with 689 stolen vehicles recovered as a result of the Flock cameras.
The vote is a remarkable turnabout from just three years ago, when the mayor and other municipal leaders urged the city council to approve the program.

The city’s wholesale rejection of these devices included Ubicquia’s so-called “smart streetlights” that worked in concert with Flock’s AI-driven automatic license plate reader (ALPR) software. This cessation of smart streetlights marks the second time in less than a decade that San Diego has experimented with and then ultimately rejected this technology.

At one point, San Diego purchased thousands of smart streetlight systems from a different vendor, GE Current, but a previous mayoral administration shuttered them in 2020. After that, Ubicquia acquired the smart city platform and proposed a newer installation of 500 cameras in 2023 in partnership with Flock—and supported by police—which was installed in 2023.

At the time, a local watchdog agency, the City of San Diego Privacy Advisory Board, asked the city council to vote down the plan. One of its board members, Pegah Parsi, wrote on LinkedIn that she is now feeling “vindication.”

“A reminder for every city, agency, and institution: if you create an advisory board of experts, listen to them!” she wrote. “Actually, earnestly listen to them. It’s cheaper than learning the hard way. Do better.”
That sentiment is echoed by Secure Justice, an Oakland-based advocacy group, which has been studying and monitoring Flock’s issues nationwide.

“We’ve documented at least 513 Flock contracts that have ended in red and blue states, in large and small cities,” Brian Hofer, the group’s executive director, emailed Ars. “It’s pretty clear that Americans do not consent to their government tracking them as we go about our daily lives.”

items.title: Yet another satellite company is jockeying for a rocket—but this one makes sense
paras: Joining forces Yet another satellite company is jockeying for a rocket—but this one makes sense “Governments need control of their critical space infrastructure, and Europe needs it most.”

11 ... ... ... A Vega C rocket lifts off from French Guiana on December 1, 2025. Credit: ESA-CNES-Arianespace/Optique Vidéo du CSG-S. Martin A Vega C rocket lifts off from French Guiana on December 1, 2025. Credit: ESA-CNES-Arianespace/Optique Vidéo du CSG-S. Martin Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced Tuesday that it is seeking to buy Italian rocket-maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion in a transaction aimed at creating Europe’s first true vertically integrated end-to-end space company.

The announcement came as an all-cash voluntary tender offer from an Italian subsidiary of ICEYE to Avio’s shareholders, led by the Italian defense conglomerate Leonardo. Avio said its board of directors “has taken note of the notice” from ICEYE and is considering the purchase offer.

Avio builds the Vega C rocket, a solid-fueled launcher designed to carry up to 3.3 metric tons (7,300 pounds) of payload to low-Earth orbit. The Vega C has flown successfully seven times in eight attempts since 2022. It is a follow-on to an earlier version of the Vega rocket that amassed a 20-for-22 record since debuting in 2012.

ICEYE is, by far, the most successful space startup in Europe, where access to private capital, regulatory barriers, and fragmented markets often hinder startup growth, according to a recent report from the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development. ICEYE’s valuation stands at more than $12 billion after the company’s most recent fundraising round in June.

In a statement, ICEYE said it wants to join forces with Avio to meet Europe’s need for “sovereign space and defense capabilities.” ICEYE manufactures and operates its own satellites for radar surveillance and sells data to commercial customers and national governments, including Ukraine, which uses ICEYE imagery for targeting and tracking Russian troop movements.

“Governments need control of their critical space infrastructure, and Europe needs it most,” said Rafal Modrzewski, CEO and co-founder of ICEYE. “Avio has built the launch and propulsion capability Europe relies on. With ICEYE’s long-term capital behind it, we can integrate the supply chain, grow output and strengthen the European programs that already depend on it. Together we can build, launch and operate sovereign space systems end-to-end, made in Europe for governments across the world.”

Avio oversees the consortium of European companies that produces the Vega C rocket and conducts final assembly of Vega C rocket stages at its factory near Rome. For most of the Vega program’s history, Avio handed the rockets to the French launch provider Arianespace, which managed marketing, sales, and launch day operations in French Guiana. Avio recently took over those responsibilities to bring the entire Vega C operation in-house.

ICEYE has built and launched 84 radar reconnaissance satellites, providing routine overhead imagery of locations around the world, even during darkness or cloud cover. In addition to its commercial satellite fleet, ICEYE has sold turnkey satellites directly to national governments, including Finland, Poland, Germany, Sweden, Portugal, Greece, and the Netherlands.

Last month, ICEYE announced a partnership with Nokia, another Finnish company, to develop a low-Earth orbit satellite constellation to support European connectivity needs, particularly in the defense and security sectors. Ukraine’s Ministry of Defense announced a preliminary agreement, saying it intends to work with ICEYE and Nokia on the constellation, days after Ukraine reported new restrictions on its access to Starlink and Starshield broadband services offered by SpaceX.
“Modern warfare has proven that reliable communications are a matter of national security,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. “We must all rely on capabilities that we can control.”

There’s a long way to go before ICEYE and Nokia can start deploying their constellation, but their goal is to begin launching 50 satellites per year starting in 2028. The companies have not disclosed expected figures for throughput and latency on the network, or a total number of satellites for global or regional coverage. Depending on altitude, it would likely require hundreds or thousands of satellites. SpaceX has more than 11,000 operating satellites in its Starlink constellation today.

What is clear, however, is that ICEYE’s future radar and broadband satellites will need rides to space, and Avio’s Vega C rocket needs business. The primary customer for Vega C is the European Space Agency, and the rest of the rocket’s future schedule is largely filled with satellites from European national governments. Vega C’s purely commercial business line is thin.

Through the proposed transaction, ICEYE says it would secure more access to launch services, and Avio would receive investment for higher production and more frequent flights of the Vega rocket family, which averages fewer than three per year.

The most recent data indicates a dedicated Vega C launch sells for approximately $55 million , just shy of the commercial price for a much more powerful dedicated SpaceX Falcon 9. Nearly all of ICEYE’s satellites, except for the first view demo spacecraft, have launched on Falcon 9 rideshare missions, which SpaceX intends to phase out after 2028. SpaceX sold rideshare launch slots for satellites of ICEYE’s size and mass for about $700,000. After accounting for potential savings after ICEYE’s potential purchase of Avio, an ICEYE satellite might be able to launch on Vega C for two to three times that price.

Avio and the European Space Agency are jointly funding the development of a new version of Vega, the Vega E, which replaces the top part of Vega C with a new higher-performing methane-fueled upper stage. ESA and Avio also signed a nearly $50 million contract last year to begin designing a reusable upper stage similar in concept and appearance to SpaceX’s Starship, although much smaller. The idea is to complete early design work on the reusable upper stage as a potential replacement for Vega E.

Business results seem to bear out the benefits of combining launch and satellite services under one roof. SpaceX’s Starlink network and Falcon 9 rocket would not have been as successful without the other. Rocket Lab, the No. 2 US launch company by launch rate, quickly branched out into satellite manufacturing after establishing the reliability of its Electron rocket. Pretty much every US launch provider has a role in satellite production or in-space services, or plans to, except for United Launch Alliance.

The coming launch crunch precipitated by SpaceX’s plans to retire the Falcon 9 has underscored the importance of assured access to space. SpaceX is prioritizing Starship launches for its own Starlink network and future Starmind AI satellites.

One of SpaceX’s competitors in the satellite broadband business, AST Space Mobile, announced last week that it is developing its own rocket to launch its communications network. It has launched most of its satellites to date on Falcon 9. Another company, Cowboy Space, plans to put orbiting data centers into space, bringing it into competition with SpaceX’s Starmind initiative. Cowboy Space, too, recently announced it was working on its own rocket.

There are reasons to disbelieve both companies’ launcher plans. Neither has any rocket development experience, and both are targeting first flights in 2028, a bewilderingly fast path to the launch pad. There are reasons to be skeptical of ICEYE and Avio, too, but if they do join forces, the combined company would boast established satellite and rocket production lines and backing from European governments seeking to reclaim sovereignty amid fraying ties with the United States.

items.title: November 18, 1990: The day Monica Seles & Gabriela Sabatini played the first five-setter in women’s tennis in 89 years
paras: On this day in tennis history, Monica Seles and Gabriela Sabatini played out a monumental match.
Look back on this historical moment in women’s tennis

On this day, November 18, 1990, Monica Seles defeated Gabriela Sabatini in the final of the Virginia Slims Championships (6-4, 5-7, 3-6, 6-4, 6-2) in a best-of-five sets final that went the distance. Seles’ triumph marked the first five-set match in women’s tennis since the 1901 US Nationals (the former name of the US Open ), when Elisabeth Moore had defeated Myrtle McAteer 6-4, 3-6, 7-5, 2-6, 6-2 in the final . For Seles, this second prestigious title, after her triumph at Roland-Garros in June, was a major step in her quest for the world No 1 ranking, a spot she would reach in March 1991.
items.impact: Although she would come back on the tour and claim a ninth and final Grand Slam title at the 1996 Australian Open, Seles would never reach the standards of her early years on the tour.

items.title: Mirra Andreeva backed to take world number one ranking from Elena Rybakina next year, ‘this is a massive moment’
paras: Mirra Andreeva won the WTA Finals to close the gap to world number one Elena Rybakina. The Russian star now trails the Kazakhstani by 293 points.

Andreeva is well-positioned to take the world number one spot in the new year, but does she really have what it takes? American ex-pros Sam Querrey and Steve Johnson have now delivered their verdicts on Andreeva’s number one chances, suggesting when she could reach the milestone.

“So [Mirra] Andreeva now is ranked two in the world. She’s only about 200 points behind [Elena] Rybakina. Remember, Rybakina won the Australian Open last year. So let’s fast-forward two months; if Rybakina doesn’t win the Australian Open and Andreeva has a good Australian Open, quarter, semi, most likely she’s going to be number one in the world,” said Querrey.

items.title: 2026 ATP Finals Day 4 Predictions Including Carlos Alcaraz vs Daniil Medvedev
paras: Alcaraz leads the head-to-head 7-3, and he has won both of their meetings indoors, including a 6-4 6-4 win in Turin in 2023 and a 6-4 7-6 win in the Vienna semifinals three weeks ago, on his way to that title.
He opened his campaign on Monday by routing Tiafoe 6-2 6-2, and he is still chasing the first ATP Finals title of his career.

Medvedev was just as comfortable in his opener, beating Cobolli 7-6 6-3 without facing a break point, and he beat Alcaraz 6-3 7-6 in the Indian Wells semifinals in March. A former champion at this event, his serve and flat groundstrokes are built for this court, but Alcaraz has solved him in seven of their ten meetings. The winner here takes control of the group and likely seals a semifinal place.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
